title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 67
paragraphs: So when all these had come to Athens, except the Parians (for the Parians had remained behind at Kythnos, waiting to see how the war would turn out) — when all the rest, I say, had arrived at Phaleron, Xerxes himself then came down to the ships, wishing to visit them and hear the opinions of those who sailed in them. When he had come and taken a conspicuous seat, the tyrants of their own nations and the divisional commanders, being summoned, came before him from their ships and took their seats in the rank the king had assigned each — first the king of Sidon, then of Tyre, and after them the rest. When they were seated in order, Xerxes sent Mardonius around, making trial of each, to ask whether he should fight a sea-battle.
